title_tag: 全球都在抢矿，中国却开始抢“垃圾”：一块废电池，为什么成了战略资源？—— 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解第1198天
h1: 全球都在抢矿，中国却开始抢“垃圾”：一块废电池，为什么成了战略资源？
category: 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解 第1198天

headline.en_html: China is turning <mark class="voc">trash</mark> into <mark class="voc">treasure</mark> on a <mark class="voc">vast</mark> scale — EV batteries, especially, will help it secure supplies of <mark class="voc">critical</mark> <mark class="voc">minerals</mark>
headline.zh: 中国正以惊人的规模，把垃圾变成宝物——尤其是电动车电池，它将帮助中国把关键矿产的供应牢牢锁定在自己手里。

notes.en: Trash means things that are no longer wanted or useful, especially household waste.
notes.ctx: 标题用 trash 不用 waste，要的是“破烂”的粗粝感——变废为宝说的就是最不起眼的东西也能翻身。
notes.ex1: Don't just throw it away as trash. 别把它当垃圾扔了。
notes.ex2: One man's trash is another man's treasure. 一个人的垃圾，是另一个人的宝贝。

notes.en: Treasure means a collection of valuable things such as gold or jewels; as a verb, to value something highly.
notes.ctx: 与 trash 押头韵，凑成“变废为宝”的英文对句，暗指废电池就是埋在城里的宝藏。
notes.ex1: We treasure these memories. 我们珍视这些记忆。
notes.ex2: The city is digging treasure out of its own rubbish. 这座城市正在从自己的垃圾里挖宝。

notes.en: Vast means extremely large in size, amount, or degree.
notes.ctx: on a vast scale＝大规模地，作者借它写出国家级体量，而不是几家工厂的生意。
notes.ex1: China is turning trash into treasure on a vast scale. 中国正在大规模地变废为宝。
notes.ex2: The scheme operates on a vast scale. 这个计划规模空前。

notes.en: Critical means extremely important, or at a point of crisis; it can also mean judging or analytical.
notes.zh: 关键的；危急的；批判性的
notes.ctx: critical minerals＝关键矿产，标题用它点出废电池里那点金属何以成了战略资源。
notes.ex1: Lithium and cobalt are critical minerals. 锂和钴是关键矿产。

notes.en: A mineral is a natural substance in the earth, such as coal, salt, or metal ore.
notes.ctx: 与第六段的 ore 是“成品对原料”：中国精炼 minerals，却进口 ores，这一对词是全文暗线。
notes.ex1: The country lacks mineral resources. 该国矿产资源匮乏。

paragraphs.en_html: A fast-growing number of EVs will soon be <mark class="voc">scrapped</mark> and replaced. Shredding their batteries <mark class="voc">yields</mark> “<mark class="voc">black mass</mark>”, a powder from which valuable metals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel can be recovered and reused. From next month the EU will make it harder to export this waste. The aim is to encourage more processing of black mass close to home (at the moment most is shipped to Asia). In August America, which has <mark class="voc">banned</mark> Chinese EVs but still imports lots of Chinese batteries, blocked all black-mass exports.
paragraphs.zh: 越来越多的电动车，很快就会报废、被换掉。把这些车的电池撕碎，就能产出“黑粉”——一种粉末，从中可以回收并再利用锂、钴、镍这些贵重的金属。从下个月起，欧盟会让这种废物的出口变得更难，目的是鼓励更多黑粉在本地加工（而目前，绝大部分都被运去了亚洲）。8月，美国封锁了所有黑粉的出口——有意思的是，这个国家禁掉了中国的电动车，却还在大量进口中国的电池。

notes.en: To scrap something means to get rid of it because it is no longer useful; as a noun, it is waste material, especially metal, that can be reused.
notes.ctx: 第一段作动词“报废”，第九段作名词“废铜废铝”，一个词两副面孔。
notes.ex1: A growing number of EVs will soon be scrapped. 越来越多的电动车很快就要报废。
notes.ex2: The plant imports scrap copper and aluminium. 这家工厂进口废铜和废铝。

notes.en: If something yields a result or a substance, it produces it; to yield can also mean to give way to pressure.
notes.ctx: 宾语决定词义：yield black mass 是“产出”，作者借此把处理垃圾悄悄写成了开采矿山。
notes.ex1: Shredding their batteries yields “black mass”. 粉碎这些电池会产出“黑粉”。
notes.ex2: The mine yields 10 tonnes of copper a day. 这座矿每天产出10吨铜。

notes.en: Black mass is the powder left after lithium-ion batteries are shredded, containing valuable metals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel.
notes.zh: 黑粉（电池粉碎后的黑色粉末）
notes.ctx: 全文主角：电池撕碎后的黑粉，富含锂钴镍，等于“城市里的矿”。
notes.ex1: Black mass might make up 20-30% of global demand for battery metals by 2050. 到2050年，黑粉可能占全球电池金属需求的20%至30%。

notes.en: To ban means to officially forbid something; to block means to stop something from moving or happening.
notes.ctx: ban 是立法层面的“禁”，block 是动作层面的“拦”：禁了中国的车，却照样买中国的电池。
notes.ex1: America has banned Chinese EVs but still imports lots of Chinese batteries. 美国禁了中国的电动车，却仍在大量进口中国的电池。

paragraphs.en_html: China, however, is unlikely to suffer. Black mass might make up 20-30% of global demand for battery metals by 2050, says the International Energy Agency, a forecaster. So China is <mark class="voc">supercharging</mark> its recycling industries: not just to <mark class="voc">shore up</mark> supplies of battery metals, but also <mark class="voc">rare-earths</mark> and much else. The goal is to make its economy less “<mark class="voc">linear</mark>” (where raw materials are made into products which are then thrown away) and more “circular” (closing the loop so recycled waste <mark class="voc">replaces</mark> raw materials).
paragraphs.zh: 不过，中国不太可能吃亏。国际能源署——一家预测机构——认为，到2050年，黑粉可能占到全球电池金属需求的二到三成。所以，中国正在给自己的回收产业猛踩油门：目标不只是稳住电池金属的供应，还有稀土，以及其他很多东西。它的目标，是让本国经济少一点“线性”（原材料被制成产品，随后被丢弃），多一点“循环”（闭合回路，让回收来的废物顶替原材料）。

notes.en: To supercharge something means to give it much more power or energy than usual.
notes.ctx: 不是“发展”，是“踩油门”，一个动词把国家意志的力度写了出来。
notes.ex1: China is supercharging its recycling industries. 中国正在给它的回收产业猛踩油门。

notes.en: To shore up something means to support or strengthen it, especially when it is weak.
notes.ctx: shore up supplies＝把电池金属的供应“顶住”，暗示这份供应本来有垮塌风险。
notes.ex1: The move aims to shore up supplies of battery metals. 此举意在巩固电池金属的供应。

notes.en: Rare earths are a group of 17 chemical elements used in magnets, batteries and electronics.
notes.ctx: 稀土其实不“稀”，难的是把 17 个化学性质相近的元素分开，中国的优势正在分离环节。
notes.ex1: China supercharges recycling of rare earths too. 中国也在加码稀土回收。

notes.en: A linear economy takes raw materials, makes products, and throws them away; a circular one closes the loop so recycled waste replaces raw materials.
notes.ctx: 全文骨架：linear 是拿料—造—扔，circular 是让回收料顶替原料。
notes.ex1: The goal is to make its economy less linear and more circular. 目标是让经济更少“线性”、更多“循环”。

notes.en: To replace A with B means to put B in the place of A; to substitute A for B means to use A in place of B.
notes.ctx: closing the loop so recycled waste replaces raw materials——用再生废料顶替原材料，正是“循环”的定义。
notes.ex1: Recycled waste replaces raw materials. 再生废料顶替了原材料。

paragraphs.en_html: Once recycling efforts were <mark class="voc">driven</mark> by concerns about pollution. Now, amid a global <mark class="voc">scramble</mark> for the materials needed to build a high-tech economy, security has become a <mark class="voc">primary</mark> <mark class="voc">motive</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 曾经，回收这件事是由“对污染的担忧”推动的。而现在，在一场为打造高科技经济所需的原材料而展开的全球争夺中，安全已经成为首要的动机。

notes.en: To drive something means to cause it to happen or to force it in a particular direction.
notes.ctx: efforts were driven by concerns——被动语态暗示回收是被外部推着走的。
notes.ex1: Once recycling efforts were driven by concerns about pollution. 过去，回收的努力是由对污染的担忧推动的。

notes.en: A scramble is a hurried and competitive struggle to get something; to scramble means to climb or move quickly using hands and feet.
notes.ctx: 不用 competition 而用 scramble，作者要说的是：这不是比赛，是抢。
notes.ex1: There is a global scramble for these materials. 全世界都在抢这些材料。

notes.en: Primary means main, most important, or happening first.
notes.ctx: a primary motive＝首要动机，比 main 更有书面语的正式感。
notes.ex1: Security has become a primary motive. 安全已成为首要动机。

notes.en: A motive is a reason for doing something, especially one that is hidden.
notes.ctx: 用 motive 不用 reason，暗含“真正推动事情的那只手未必明说”。
notes.ex1: Security has become a primary motive. 安全已成为首要动机。

paragraphs.en_html: In the 1980s China started to import waste, taking the <mark class="voc">hardware</mark>, paper and plastic that richer countries did not want. A <mark class="voc">sprawling</mark> informal recycling-sector emerged, led by <mark class="voc">scavengers</mark> picking through rubbish piles. Much ended up in <mark class="voc">landfills</mark> or burnt in the open air, <mark class="voc">leaching</mark> toxic chemicals and creating poisonous <mark class="voc">smog</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 20 世纪80 年代，中国开始进口废物，接收那些富裕国家不要的金属器件、纸张和塑料。一个杂乱蔓延的非正规回收行业应运而生，主角是在垃圾堆里翻捡的拾荒者。这些废物中的大部分，最终进了填埋场，或者索性被露天焚烧，渗出有毒的化学物质，制造出有毒的烟雾。

notes.en: Hardware means tools and equipment made of metal; in computing, it means the physical parts of a computer.
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义：这里指一船一船的金属器件，不是电脑硬件。
notes.ex1: They took the hardware, paper and plastic that richer countries did not want. 他们把富国不要的五金件、纸张和塑料拉了回来。

notes.en: Sprawling means spreading out over a large area in an untidy or irregular way.
notes.zh: 杂乱蔓延的，无序扩张的
notes.ctx: 不是普通的“大”，是“大得没规矩、东一块西一块”。
notes.ex1: A sprawling informal recycling sector emerged. 一个杂乱蔓延的非正规回收业冒了出来。

notes.en: A scavenger is a person or animal that collects things that have been discarded, or feeds on dead animals.
notes.ctx: 不用 worker、不用 recycler，一个词写尽这条链上“我们翻剩下的”位置。
notes.ex1: … led by scavengers picking through rubbish piles. ……带头的是在垃圾堆里翻找的拾荒者。

notes.en: A landfill is a large place where waste is buried under the ground.
notes.ctx: 全文“三种去向”之一：填埋、焚烧、回收，后面每段都会回指一次。
notes.ex1: Much of it ended up in landfills. 其中大部分进了填埋场。

notes.en: If a liquid leaches, it slowly passes through soil or waste, carrying chemicals with it.
notes.ctx: 现在分词作结果状语：一埋一烧，结果就是渗毒、冒烟。
notes.ex1: … leaching toxic chemicals and creating poisonous smog. ……沥滤出有毒化学品，制造出有毒的烟雾。

notes.en: Smog is a form of air pollution that looks like thick smoke mixed with fog.
notes.ctx: smoke+fog 的混成词，把八十年代遮天蔽日的画面直接压在读者眼前。
notes.ex1: Rubbish burnt in the open air created poisonous smog. 露天焚烧垃圾制造出有毒的烟雾。

paragraphs.en_html: China is still <mark class="voc">well behind</mark> <mark class="voc">squeaky-clean</mark> European countries when it comes to waste management (though it is hard to say how far, as it does not publish detailed national data for recycling). Its poorer rural areas are still often <mark class="voc">strewn with</mark> rubbish. But officials have made China’s big cities, at least, cleaner and more pleasant to live in. Now their focus is shifting to the use of recycling <mark class="voc">for the sake of</mark> security. In July China released a plan for the development of the circular economy until 2030. “The importance of resource security has become increasingly <mark class="voc">prominent</mark>, while geopolitical dynamics…have grown complex and severe,” the plan noted.
paragraphs.zh: 在废物管理这件事上，中国仍然远远落后于那些一尘不染的欧洲国家（不过到底落后多少，很难说清，因为中国并不公布关于回收的详细全国数据）。它较为贫困的农村地区，至今仍常常垃圾遍地。但至少，官员们让中国的大城市变得更干净、也更宜居了。而现在，他们的重心正在转移——为了安全而利用回收。今年 7 月，中国发布了一份面向2030 年的循环经济发展规划。该规划指出：“资源安全的重要性日益凸显，而地缘政治的……已经变得复杂而严峻。”

notes.en: Well behind means much further back than something — here “well” is a degree adverb meaning much.
notes.ctx: well 这里是程度副词＝much，不是“好”；同一串还有 well ahead、well above。
notes.ex1: China is still well behind European countries. 中国仍然远远落后于欧洲国家。

notes.en: Squeaky-clean means very clean; it can also mean having a spotless reputation.
notes.zh: 干净得发亮的；名声清白的
notes.ctx: 与 well behind 形成反差：中国远远落后于“擦得吱吱响”的欧洲。
notes.ex1: … behind squeaky-clean European countries. ……落后于干净得吱吱响的欧洲国家。

notes.en: To strew means to scatter things over a surface; strewn with means covered with things scattered around.
notes.ctx: 作者写的不是“脏”，是“乱”——东西东一堆西一摊地撒在那里。
notes.ex1: Rural areas are still strewn with rubbish. 农村地区仍然散落着垃圾。

notes.en: For the sake of means for the purpose of, or for the benefit of, something.
notes.ctx: for the sake of security——回收的目的被改写成“安全”，这是全文的转折。
notes.ex1: Their focus is shifting to the use of recycling for the sake of security. 它们的重心正转向为了安全而使用回收。

notes.en: Prominent means important, well-known, or easily noticed.
notes.ctx: 官方文件里 resource security has become increasingly prominent，标准的公文腔，原样引进。
notes.ex1: The importance of resource security has become increasingly prominent. 资源安全的重要性日益凸显。
